bot_token.description: Telegram bot token (BotFather). Deprecated, removed in 0.63.0: name a grant in bot_token_grant_id instead (#801).

bot_token_grant_id.description: The grant under which the vault delivers the bot token sealed (GH #1059, #801). Set, `bot_token` is ignored and the cell polls only once the box is opened. Never empty here: an empty grant beside an empty `bot_token` is refused at parse. Immutable.

long_poll_request_secs.description: Telegram-side getUpdates long-poll wait in seconds

max_document_bytes.description: The largest document the connector downloads, in bytes (20 MiB, the Bot API's own getFile limit; the document is committed to the colony blob store and the turn carries only its reference in attachments[]); a larger one reaches the turn as its caption plus `[file "<name>" could not be stored: document too large]`. Set at birth

messages.description: messages is not required at the substrate (GH #1061): the sealed credential box reaches this cell with body.sealed alone, and a required key here would refuse it at delivery as consumes_violation; the cell itself still refuses a send without it.

chat_id.description: chat_id is not required at the substrate (GH #1061): the sealed credential box reaches this cell with body.sealed alone, and a required key here would refuse it at delivery as consumes_violation; the cell itself still refuses a send without it.

description.purpose: One Telegram chat as one cell. Inbound chat messages emerge as one user-origin turn each; a finished turn arriving from the topology is written back into the chat it came from. The cell is the plain Telegram proxy with one deliberate difference: params.emit_to points one level up (..), because every emission is routed by the edges of the level that holds this connector (the substrate applies apply_edges to a source emission too; emit_to is only the no-route address).
description.use_when: Wherever a topology needs a Telegram surface in front of something ELSE. One instance per bot token. Wire the cell itself -- there is no hive and no lane name to hit: an emission carrying hop.error_code is the connector's own failure, one without it is an inbound turn.
description.not_in_scope: Does not understand bot commands, does not keep chat history, does not transform messages beyond extracting text and identifiers. The connector no longer normalises its own output onto turn/error; the level that holds it does, and that level is channels (GH #303).
description.emits_meaning: Two emission shapes, hence no required hop fields: (a) source emission -- one user-origin text turn per inbound Telegram message, hop carries chat_id/user_id/message_id/platform (promote chat_id to context on the out-edge, or it dies with the next cell emission); (b) inbound-error emission (missing_chat_id/missing_assistant_turn/send_failed/invalid_body) -- empty messages[], hop carries error_code + msg_type 'proxy_inbound_error', targeted at reply_to. Declaring chat_id/platform as required breaks shape (b) against the substrate emits validation.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: the last assistant turn is sent to the chat. context.chat_id selects the target Telegram chat (promoted onto context by the out-edge of the level that holds this connector).
examples: Inbound Telegram 'Hi' -> emit body { messages: [{ origin: 'user', type: 'text', text: 'Hi' }] }, hop { platform: 'telegram', chat_id: 12345, user_id: 67890 }
